errata.error: The EA's Holyhead readings are erratic from 1 to 20 February 2026. Of the 1,920 values the store holds, 357 read between 3.95 and 8.94 m AOD and 148 sit at the −3.05 m floor, while the highest water at Holyhead in the rest of 2026 outside 8 to 13 April is 3.46 m.
errata.response: 1 to 20 February 2026 is flagged `suspect`, keeping the EA's own flag as `source_flag`. Spans are whole days, so the readings between the erratic ones are flagged with them.
errata.evidence: Found by running GESLA's datum-jump rule (`datumJumps` in `src/sources/gesla`, a 30-day median shift of more than 0.75 m) over every record the store lists as coastal, and read back in November 2026 value by value. The readings agree with CMEMS's Holyhead (`cmems/Holyhead`) at −3.05 m, its datum difference, through 31 January, so the EA's gauge isn't off by a constant. They go wrong from 01:15 UTC on 1 February to 01:45 UTC on 20 February, and agree again from 21 February. CMEMS's copy of the gauge carries the same readings. BODC's record of the gauge (`bodc/hol`), whose values stay between 0.4 and 6.2 m chart datum on those days, follows a tide that neaps on 10 February and springs on 19 February.

errata.error: The EA's Holyhead readings are erratic again on 8, 9, 10, 13 and 14 April 2026: 204 of the 654 values from 8 to 14 April read above 3.95 m AOD, up to 8.27 m, or sit at the −3.05 m floor. The readings of 11 and 12 April follow the tide.
errata.response: 8 to 14 April 2026 is flagged `suspect`, keeping the EA's own flag as `source_flag`. QC flags 196 of the 204 erratic values, so the span flags the other 8 and the readings between them.
errata.evidence: Found in November 2026 while reading back erratum `ea-holyhead-2026-erratic`, by counting the readings above 3.95 m AOD or at the floor: the highest water at Holyhead in the rest of 2026 is 3.46 m. None of 11 and 12 April's 187 readings is beyond. CMEMS's copy of the gauge (`cmems/Holyhead`) also has erratic values on 10 April.

errata.error: The EA's Washpile levels are 3.1 to 3.2 m higher against neighboring gauges from 5 April 2026 than they were up to 3 February, through the last values the store holds, on 30 April 2026. The gauge has no readings in between (erratum `ea-washpile-2026-gap`), so the shift can't be dated more closely.
errata.response: Values from 5 April 2026 on are flagged `suspect`, keeping the EA's own flag as `source_flag`, until the EA says the gauge is right again.
errata.evidence: Found by running GESLA's datum-jump rule (`datumJumps` in `src/sources/gesla`, a 30-day median shift of more than 0.75 m) over every record the store lists as coastal, and confirmed, November 2026, by hourly differences against three EA gauges within 115 km (`ea/E71239`, `ea/E71124`, `ea/E70039`). Washpile less each of them has medians of 0.04, −3.82 and −0.01 m through 3 February and 3.22, −0.58 and 3.11 m from 5 April, shifts of 3.18, 3.24 and 3.12 m. Monthly medians are 0.25 m in January, −0.09 m in February and 3.39 m in April. The last values, on 30 April, read 29.797 m.

errata.error: The EA has no readings for Washpile after 06:00 UTC on 3 February to 4 April 2026. The store holds five values in between, at 17 March 12:17 and 12:23, 22 March 12:42 and 1 April 12:57 and 15:53, none on a quarter hour. The EA's archive has no E71339 reading on 14 of the 60 days from 4 February to 4 April, and has 96 on 5 April.
errata.response: The store keeps what the EA serves and leaves the gap.
errata.evidence: Read from the EA's daily archive files in November 2026: `GET /archive/readings-<day>.csv` for 14 of the 60 days from 4 February to 4 April, none of which has a row for E71339, and for 5 April, which has 96. The other days weren't read. 3 February's file has 25 rows, to 06:00 UTC.

errata.error: The EA's Dover levels sit about 4.6 m low from 29 May to 18 June 2026.
errata.response: 29 May to 18 June 2026 is flagged `suspect`, keeping the EA's own flag as `source_flag`. The store's QC already flags the gauge's values from 19 June to 31 August.
errata.evidence: Found by running GESLA's datum-jump rule (`datumJumps` in `src/sources/gesla`, a 30-day median shift of more than 0.75 m) over every record the store lists as coastal, and confirmed, November 2026, by daily-mean differences against REFMAR's Calais (`refmar/55`) and Boulogne-sur-Mer (`refmar/111`): the differences are −3.84 and −4.78 m before and after the span and −8.41 and −9.37 m over it.
